chunks: By this chain of narration, he said: Al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) used to supplicate with this supplication:

My God! How can I call upon You when I have disobeyed You? And how can I not call upon You when You know of my love for You in my heart! Even if I have been disobedient, I stretch toward You a hand full of sins, and an eye extended with hope.
My Master! You are the Greatest of the great, and I am the prisoner of the prisoners. I am a prisoner of my sin, ransomed by my crime.

My God! If You seek me for my sin, then I shall seek You by Your benevolence. If You seek me for my crime, then I shall seek You by Your pardon. If You order me to the Fire, then I shall tell its inhabitants that I used to say: There is no god but Allah, Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah.
O Allah! Obedience gladdens You, and disobedience does not harm You, so grant me what gladdens You, and forgive me of what does not harm You, O Most Merciful of the merciful ones.

key_terms.دعاء: Du'a: supplication, prayer of invocation addressed directly to God
key_terms.عفو: Afw: pardon, God's act of effacing and forgiving sins
key_terms.كرم: Karam: generosity, benevolence, noble character of God
key_terms.مرتهن: Murtahan: ransomed, held in pledge or mortgage for one's sins

ai.seo_question: What is the supplication of Imam Sadiq about calling upon God despite disobedience?
ai.summary: This is a supplication that Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq (AS) used to recite regularly, expressing the paradox of a sinner calling upon God: though the servant's hands are full of sin, his heart is full of love and hope. The du'a boldly appeals to God's generosity and pardon, arguing that if God demands accountability for sins, the servant will demand God's own attributes of benevolence and forgiveness in return. It concludes with a profound theological insight that God's nature is not harmed by human disobedience, so forgiveness costs Him nothing.
